text:
marta: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC session — we need a small, concrete plan for Triton vs CUTLASS kernel usage in the serving runtime before sprint planning. My gut: Triton for new attention variants (flexible kernels), CUTLASS for rock-solid matmul paths. Need perf targets, testing checklist, and an owner for the compatibility shim. Who can take this?

sanjay: I can prototype a thin Triton wrapper, but we should be explicit about binary size and runtime deps. Triton bundles + python dev workflow complicates Dedicated/Private installs.

anya: +1 on ownership concerns. Also want to avoid exploding CI times. Can we gate Triton-only tests behind a matrix flag?

noah: Agree on gating. Proposal for selector API (sketch):
```
// runtime kernel selector (pseudo)
interface KernelSelector {
  choose(op, shape, dtype, hw) -> KernelVariant  // returns {backend: 'triton'|'cutlass', variant_id}
  validate_variant(variant_id) -> {pass: bool, metrics} // perf + numeric checks
}
```
Selector behavior: prefer Triton for attention ops when seq_len <= 1024 and batch small (fast custom attention), else prefer CUTLASS for large matmuls. Fallback path must be fast (no compile-on-demand in hot path).

samira: On the attention side: we need flash-attention-style memory layout tests and numeric regression checks for quantized modes (nf4/int8). Some Triton kernels are great for fused attention, but we saw accuracy drift at 8-bit in prior experiments. Add small evaluation harness that replays a stable prompt set and checks cosine similarity / token-level divergence.

ci-bot: nightly-kernel-matrix: full-triton: FAILED (H100, seq=2048, nf4) - see /ci/artifacts/1768239000/logs

marta: Thanks, CI failure noted. That points to two immediate items: 1) perf matrix doc with hw rows (A100/H100), seq lens (128/512/2048), dtypes (fp16, nf4, int8), and target tokens/sec + memory; 2) a numeric-regression harness integrated into PR checks that runs a small golden prompt set.

sanjay: I'll own the Triton wrapper POC. Plan: minimal runtime boundary (C ABI) + prebuilt wheel for hosted, and a fallback pure-CUDA/CUTLASS path for Private. ETA: end of week for prototype.

anya: I'll add CI matrix toggles and a new label `kernel-rfci` so we can run heavy tests only on durable commits. Also will add an artifacts collector for numeric diffs.

noah: I'll draft the KernelSelector API in the runtime repo (RFC PR) and include hooks for: policy rules, perf-history lookup, and cold-start compile avoidance. Also adding an in-memory cache of chosen variant per model-version to keep decisions fast.

samira: I'll prepare the prompt set and numeric acceptance criteria: per-token KL < 1e-3 and embedding cosine > 0.995 for quantized variants. Also will write a small microbench harness that runs attention kernels in isolation (to detect fragmentation or workspace issues).

marta: Nice. Let's capture these as discrete TODOs so we can close out at sprint planning: 
- perf-matrix doc (owner: marta)
- Triton wrapper POC + packaging plan (owner: sanjay)
- KernelSelector RFC + selector cache (owner: noah)
- CI matrix toggle + artifact collector (owner: anya)
- numeric harness + golden prompts + acceptance thresholds (owner: samira)

sanjay: For the Triton wrapper, question: do we want AOT-compiled Triton kernels (prebuild images) or JIT at runtime? My vote: prebuild for hosted, optional JIT in dev images only. Avoid JIT in production to keep latency predictable.

noah: +1 prebuild. Add a compatibility tag per kernel that contains (seq_range, dtype_support, required_sm). Selector can quickly filter by compatibility tags.

anya: I'll add a CI job that runs prebuilt-kernel smoke tests during the release pipeline.

marta: Timeline check: can we have the perf-matrix and KernelSelector RFC by Tuesday? If so we can slot the prototype and CI items into the sprint.

sanjay: Tuesday for a short POC writeup + CI failing example. Prototype code later in sprint.

noah: RFC draft by Tuesday EOD.

samira: golden prompts ready by Tuesday morning.

marta: Perfect. Last note: document the safety net for failing numeric checks — automatic fallback to CUTLASS + rollout blocker flag. We should make the rollout conservative (canary then ramp).

anya: I'll add the rollout policy YAML snippet to the console docs so solutions teams understand how to opt-in/out.

marta: Great. Thanks all — I'll create the perf-matrix doc and the initial checklist. If anyone finds additional CI failures, drop artifacts here. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: linked-artifact /ci/artifacts/1768241001/kernel-failure-logs.zip

sanjay: ack, I'll dig in and try to reproduce locally on H100 sim.

noah: I'll wire up a small tracer to log selector decisions in staged environments so we can validate behavior in Dedicated.

marta: closing loop — meeting on Monday to review progress. If anything blocks, mention @marta and we'll triage.
